approach: Sliding Window (Two Pointers) algorithm to dynamically find the shortest window containing all distinct characters.
observation: The set of total distinct characters in S is fixed. Expanding the right pointer adds characters to our window map, while incrementing the left pointer shrinks the window while all distinct characters remain present.
bruteForce: Check all possible substrings O(N^2) and check if each contains all distinct characters. Total time complexity O(N^3) or O(N^2).
optimalSolution: Use sliding window: maintain left and right pointers. Expand right, update frequency map. Whenever map.size() equals total distinct count, record window size right - left + 1, then increment left and shrink frequency map until valid condition breaks.
timeComplexity: O(N) where N is the length of string S.
spaceComplexity: O(26) auxiliary space for frequency tracking.
dryRun: S = 'aabcbcdbca'. Distinct count = 4 ('a', 'b', 'c', 'd'). Window expands right until 'dbca' at right=9, left=6. map.size() == 4. Min length = 4.
edgeCases: String already has all unique chars ('abcd')
